title: Rhombus_Botnet_Investigation_ea6
description: Investigate and respond to a Rhombus botnet infection on compromised systems within your network.

levels.title: Introduction
levels.content: The Rhombus botnet is a Linux DDoS botnet that targets VPS and IoT devices. It includes persistence mechanisms and acts as a dropper for additional malware payloads. Your task is to investigate and respond to a Rhombus botnet infection on compromised systems within your network. You will need to identify suspicious services, abnormal network traffic, and persistence mechanisms.

levels.title: Get Access
levels.cloud_content:
You have SSH access to the bot1 host with the following credentials:
- Username: cyrano
- Password: cyrano
levels.local_content: Local sandbox access is not required for this scenario.

levels.title: Identify Suspicious Service
levels.content:
Identify and investigate an unauthorized or suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication.

**Question:** What is the name of the suspicious service responsible for periodic external communication?
levels.solution: Check running services and look for any unusual or unfamiliar services that might be communicating with external hosts. The suspicious service is likely named `bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check running services and look for any unusual or unfamiliar services that might be communicating with external hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are scheduled to run periodically and communicate with external hosts.

levels.title: Identify Abnormal Network Traffic Service
levels.content:
Identify the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic.

**Question:** What is the name of the service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic?
levels.solution: Investigate network connections and look for services that are sending a high volume of traffic to external hosts. The service responsible for generating abnormal volumes of network traffic is likely named `bot-flood-RHOMBUS.service`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Investigate network connections and look for services that are sending a high volume of traffic to external hosts.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for services that are sending a high volume of traffic to the target host `192.168.80.100` on port `8888`.

levels.title: Determine Persistence Mechanism
levels.content:
Determine how the suspicious service is automatically started after reboot.

**Question:** What is the persistence mechanism used by the suspicious service?
levels.solution: Check systemd timers and services to identify how the suspicious service is scheduled to run automatically. The persistence mechanism is likely a systemd timer named `bot-beacon-RHOMBUS.timer`.

hints.title: First hint title
hints.content: Check systemd timers and services to identify how the suspicious service is scheduled to run automatically.

hints.title: Second hint title
hints.content: Look for systemd timers that are scheduled to run periodically and start the suspicious service.
